source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed whenever another person requests health information, because they receive the same disclosure treatment as routine records.","B":"Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed freely for treatment purposes, because HIPAA never requires authorization when information is requested by another clinician.","C":"Psychotherapy notes receive special protection, and with limited exceptions HIPAA generally requires patient authorization before they are disclosed in most cases.","D":"Psychotherapy notes fall outside HIPAA because they are kept separately from the medical record, so federal privacy requirements do not apply to their release at all."}}
source_row.rationale: HHS explains that psychotherapy notes are specially protected and generally require patient authorization before disclosure, subject to limited exceptions. Option C states that rule. Option A incorrectly treats psychotherapy notes like routine records. Option B incorrectly assumes treatment-purpose disclosure is automatically allowed to another clinician. Option D incorrectly claims that separate storage removes the notes from HIPAA protection.
source_row.source_detail: 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2) / HHS HIPAA guidance on psychotherapy notes: authorization is generally required for use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes, subject to limited enumerated exceptions; psychotherapy notes receive protections beyond ordinary medical records. Current HIPAA Privacy Rule and HHS guidance; medical-record guidance last reviewed 2025-05-30 and regulation currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, continuity, confidentiality, quality/cost-effective care, legal/ethical rights and assignment/delegation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: HHS — HIPAA Privacy Rule: Psychotherapy Notes
source_row.stem: A family member asks a clinician to release separately maintained psychotherapy notes without the patient's authorization. Which HIPAA principle is most accurate?
